meta.title: Blincho | A little pause. A better rhythm.
meta.description: Free screen breaks for macOS, Windows and Linux. Activity timelines, call-aware reminders, tray previews, optional camera checks and local MCP, in 30 languages.
brand.name: Blincho

hero.title:
A little pause.

hero.intro: Meet Blincho, your free screen-break companion. Reminders adapt to your activity and calls, while local statistics help you understand your day.
hero.note: Free to use. Every feature included.

how.eyebrow: A rhythm that fits real life
how.title:
There when you need a nudge.
Quiet when you step away.
how.intro: Your day does not move like a stopwatch. Blincho makes space for the way you actually use your computer.
how.step1.title: Settle into your work
how.step1.body: Blincho keeps track of active screen time, so your next pause follows the time you spend at your computer.
how.step2.title: Take a small pause
how.step2.body: A reminder gives you a moment to look away. Explore the included exercises for something different to try.
how.step3.title: Step away, without the timer
how.step3.body: Break timing pauses when you are away, your screen is locked or your computer is asleep.
features.title:
Small pauses.
Plenty of possibilities.
features.exercises.title: A change of focus
features.exercises.body: Follow guided exercises, explore ergonomics tips and keep a personal comfort journal alongside your breaks.
features.stats.title: See your rhythm
features.stats.body: Browse daily timelines of work, absence, lock, sleep, pauses and rest. Compare work sessions and weekly averages, with gaps in older records clearly marked.
features.personal.title: Feel at home
features.personal.body: Set work and break durations, choose strict breaks, adjust sounds and notifications, and pick a light, dark or system theme.
features.languages.title: In your own words
features.languages.body: Use Blincho in any of 30 languages, including right-to-left Arabic.

faq.title: Before your first pause.
faq.free.a: Yes. Every feature is free to use, with no paid tier.
faq.activity.q: What happens when I leave my computer?
faq.activity.a: Blincho pauses break timing when you are away, your screen is locked or your computer is asleep, then continues when you return.
faq.platform.a: Builds are available for macOS, Windows and Linux. Windows and Linux behavior on real hardware has not yet been verified. Pick the architecture and package that match your computer.
faq.settings.q: Can I make it fit my routine?
faq.settings.a: Yes. You can adjust break preferences, choose a theme and switch between 30 languages in the app.
footer.tagline: A little space in your screen day.
download.preparing: Downloads are being prepared. Check releases for progress.
release.1.3.2: A calmer compact interface, 15 languages, light and dark themes, and clearer break notifications. Activity, lock and sleep handling includes automated regression checks.
privacy.title: Your data stays yours
privacy.body: Blincho keeps settings, activity history, comfort journal answers and optional call history on your device. Call history is off by default, stores only observed times and app names, and can be deleted separately. Camera checks are off by default; frames are processed locally and never saved or uploaded. Local MCP is off by default and shares settings, timer status and aggregate statistics only with an authenticated local client, excluding detailed activity, call names, journal answers and frames. Unless you turn update checks off, the app contacts blincho.app for version information; downloads come from GitHub. These requests do not send your activity history or journal answers. This website stores only your language and theme choices and uses no advertising or analytics scripts. Hosting and download providers receive ordinary connection data.
release.1.3.3: A calmer compact interface, 15 languages, light and dark themes, and clearer break notifications. Activity, lock and sleep handling includes automated regression checks.
release.1.4.1: 30 interface languages, including Armenian, and update preferences for supported desktop packages. Choose automatic updates, ask before downloading, or turn off background update checks.
release.1.5.0: macOS now uses Tauri with a native timer and imports existing local history. Windows and Linux keep Electron. macOS updates remain manual.
release.1.5.1: macOS now uses Tauri with a native timer and imports existing local history. Windows and Linux keep Electron. macOS updates remain manual.
release.1.5.2: macOS now uses Tauri with a native timer and imports existing local history. Windows and Linux keep Electron. macOS updates remain manual.
release.1.6.0: All desktop versions now use Rust and Tauri, including Windows and Linux on x64 and ARM64. Existing history is imported once. Updates are installed manually.
features.calls.title: Let the call finish
features.calls.body: Enable call-aware reminders to postpone breaks by five minutes while a call is detected, even in strict mode. Optional local call history shows app names, durations and daily and weekly totals. Detection is approximate; recording is off by default.
features.tray.title: A glance, then back to work
features.tray.body: See the next break, today's work time and completed breaks without opening the main window. macOS and Windows offer a hover preview; Linux shows a live tray menu. A phone badge marks a detected call.
features.camera.title: An optional check after a break
features.camera.body: Turn on camera presence checks to lock the computer if no person is detected after a timed break. Off by default and requires camera access. Frames stay on your device and are never saved or uploaded. If the check is unavailable, Blincho skips locking.
features.mcp.title: Connect your AI assistant
features.mcp.body: Enable local MCP to share timer status and aggregate statistics by day, week or date range, and request timer actions. Off by default, protected by an access token and available only on your computer. Detailed activity, call names, journal answers and camera frames are excluded.
faq.calls.a: You can enable call postponement in Settings. A detected call delays an automatic break by five minutes, including in strict mode, then Blincho checks again. Detection uses approximate system signals; browser calls identify the browser. Saving call history is a separate choice and is off by default.
faq.camera.q: Do I need to use the camera or connect an AI client?
faq.camera.a: No. Camera checks and local MCP are separate optional features, both off by default. Normal break reminders work without them. Enabling camera checks requests access and processes frames only on your device. Enable MCP only for a local client you trust and keep its access token private.
release.1.7.1: Tray previews and detailed daily activity timelines, with work sessions, rest intervals and weekly averages. History stays on your device.
release.1.7.2: Optional local call history with app names, durations, daily timelines and weekly totals. Recording is off by default and stores no conversation content.
release.1.7.3: A phone badge and live tray status show detected calls. Call status works separately from voluntary call-history recording.
release.1.8.0: Optional local camera presence checks and computer locking, with frames processed on the device and never saved or uploaded. Later releases run the check only after a timed break finishes.
release.1.8.14: Optional local MCP connects AI clients to timer status, settings, today's totals and timer actions. Camera presence checks run only after the timed break finishes.
release.1.8.15: Local MCP now reports statistics by day, calendar week or date range, with available-data dates and visible gaps. Window position and size are preserved after lock, sleep and breaks.
